{{Quote|Although my travels did not take me to the howler's homeworld of Peridea—apparently it exists far beyond the known galaxy—legends of these remarkable beasts have traveled across the stars.|From the journal of [[Ardis San Tekka]].|<ref name="Bestiary" />}}
'''Howlers''' were [[extragalactic]] [[hair|furred]] quadrupedal [[species|creatures]] [[Homeworld|native]] to the [[planet]] [[Peridea]]. Howlers could be tamed and ridden, and would respond to commands as demonstrated by [[Enoch]] and [[Sabine Wren]], who used the word "tota" to order [[Sabine Wren's howler|one such creature]] to sit.<ref name="Far Far Away" /> 

Howlers were also ridden by a [[Bandits of Peridea|group of bandits]] that resided on Peridea.<ref name="Far Far Away" /> These bandits rode the creatures into battle when they attacked Sabine Wren, [[Ezra Bridger]], and a group of [[Noti]] nomads.<ref name="Dreams and Madness" />

==Behavior==
[[File:AkaCover-Ahsoka6.png|thumb|left|250px|Sabine Wren rides a howler]]
An [[extragalactic]] [[species]]<ref name="Far Far Away" /> of [[canine]]s that inhabited the barren wilderness<ref name="Databank" /> of wastelands and [[grass]]lands that made up the planet [[Peridea]],<ref name="SWECG" /> howlers were [[Sentience|non-sentient]], quadrupedal animals<ref name="Bestiary" /> with shaggy [[Color|brown]]<ref name="Databank" /> or white fur.<ref name="Dreams and Madness" />

Howlers exhibited extreme loyalty, with [[Sabine Wren's howler|one]] refusing to part with its rider, [[Sabine Wren]], even though they had only recently met and despite her scolding it and insisting it leave her alone.<ref name="Far Far Away" /> Indeed, howlers thrived on interactions and sought out the approval of the whatever creature they saw as the alpha.<ref name="Bestiary" /> While it would take patience, howlers could be domesticated and would become devoted companions to their tamer. In particular, howlers grew attached to masters who were kind to them.<ref name="SWECG" /> They would also display signs of aggression, becoming agitated towards unfamiliar beings. That behavior frightened members of the [[Noti]] [[species]], who shared a [[homeworld]] with the howlers.<ref name="Far Far Away" />
